walkthroughs.body_html:
Practical Skills — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Practical Skills brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Practical Skills.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of a control variable in an enzyme experiment?
options: pH
Rate of reaction
Independent variable
Time taken

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.

mcqs.q: In osmosis, which direction does water move?
options: Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
From a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution) to lower water potential.
Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
Water moves from high solute concentration to low solute concentration.

mcqs.q: How does myelination increase the speed of nerve impulse conduction?
options: Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
Action potentials jump between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction), skipping the myelinated sections.
Myelin makes the axon thicker so the signal travels faster through more material.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
